notes: Tier 1 (direct HTTP fetch) sufficed throughout; no block encountered, Playwright/Chrome not needed. robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow (checked first). METHOD: fetched homepage https://www.myer.com.au/ and extracted the embedded __NEXT_DATA__ React-Query cache, which contains the site's FULL live category/nav tree (queryKey ['catalogue'], ~28.6k lines, all departments incl. Home id=17940). Walked the entire 'Home' department subtree top to bottom (Kitchen Appliances, Dining, Home Decor, Bathroom, Bedding, Furniture, Outdoor, Food & Hampers, Personal Care, Books & Stationery, Top Brands, Now Trending, New) looking for any node whose DESCRIPTION (not just SEO title) names a holiday. RESULT: zero Christmas/Halloween/Diwali/Easter/Valentine/Thanksgiving/New-Year category nodes exist in the current live nav tree under Home. Two near-misses investigated and excluded: (1) 'Hampers & Gift Packs' (seoToken christmas-hampers--1, id 730184) and its Food & Hampers siblings (Drinks, Savoury Snacks, Sweet Treats, Biscuits, Confectionery, Cakes) all carry an SEO meta <title> beginning 'Christmas ...' but their actual category 'description' (display name) is generic and year-round (e.g. 'Hampers & Gift Packs', 'Sweet Treats') -- confirmed by fetching the Hampers PLP live (61 products, category.description='Hampers & Gift Packs', only the SEO title says Christmas). This is boilerplate SEO title noise, not genuine holiday categorization, so excluded per the 'category merely contains seasonal products' rule. (2) 'Spring Home Shop' (seoToken seasonal-shop, id 1630574, under Now Trending) is a weather-season (Spring) landing page, not a holiday/festival -- excluded. Also found 'Lunar New Year' (id 777502) but it lives under the Gifts department (Gifts > Gifts by Interest > Lunar New Year), not Home, so out of this task's Home/Homewares scope -- not investigated further, no top-level cross-department Christmas/seasonal hub exists in the main nav to justify following it. TOP-LEVEL NAV confirmed to be: New In, Women, Men, Beauty, Home, Travel & Tech, Kids, Toys, Gifts, Sale, MYER one -- no dedicated Christmas/seasonal hub at top level. Because the site is 'known for elaborate Christmas homewares' per task brief, did NOT stop at nav-absence: downloaded https://www.myer.com.au/sitemap/buy-sitemap.xml (a Screaming-Frog-generated SEO keyword-landing-page sitemap) and grepped for christmas/halloween/diwali/easter/valentine/thanksgiving/new-year -- found only Christmas SEO pages (e.g. /buy/christmas-decorations-santa) plus one unrelated /buy/halloween-dress (fashion, out of scope). Opened /buy/christmas-decorations-santa: this is an internal-search-backed keyword landing page (not real taxonomy), but its embedded 'trending searches' JSON leaked real category URLs for an orphaned category cluster named 'The Christmas Shop' (internal name s_home_the-christmas-shop), reachable at /c/home/the-christmas-shop--1/<slug>. IMPORTANT: this cluster is completely absent from the main catalogue/nav tree (confirmed by grep -c on the full nav JSON = 0 matches) -- i.e. it is not clickable from any menu on the live site, only discoverable via sitemap/search-suggestion archaeology, exactly as the task's absence-proof rule anticipates. Probed every URL variant found (individual/trees-accessories/christmas-decoration-packs/home-christmas-decorations/wreaths-garlands all 404 under /home/); three resolve live (200) under /c/home/the-christmas-shop--1/: (a) xmas-home-decorations -> category.description 'Christmas Home Décor', productTotalCount 1, sole product is a genuine Christmas garland (Christabelle Alpine Snow Christmas Garland) -- INCLUDED, flagged. (b) christmas-tree-decorations -> category.description 'Christmas Tree Decorations', productTotalCount 1, sole product genuinely Christmas (Christabelle Gold Glass Baubles, merchCategory 'CHRISTMS TRIM') -- INCLUDED, flagged. (c) shop-by-christmas-theme -> category.description 'Christmas Collections', productTotalCount 65; inspected the full embedded productList (48 of 65 rows) and only ~4 items were genuinely Christmas-tagged (merchCategory 'Home/Christmas Trim'); the other ~44 were plain dinnerware/glassware (Dinner Sets, Tumblers, Wine Glasses, merchCategory 'Home/Tabletop') with no Christmas association -- this is a broken/stale merchandising rule serving mostly unrelated catalog content under a Christmas-named page, so EXCLUDED per the 'genuine holiday association' rule despite its Christmas-sounding description. A parallel instance of the same cluster also exists under /c/gifts/the-christmas-shop--1/... (Gifts department, disallowed by robots.txt and out of Home scope) -- not crawled, noted only to confirm the hub spans departments. Qty method used: structured/API count from the SSR-embedded React-Query cache, JSON path props.pageProps.dehydratedState.queries[key=['category',...]].state.data.productTotalCount -- this is the live site's own reported total, not estimated. Both included rows carry MANUAL REVIEW flags because the pages are technically live/genuine but orphaned from current navigation and show extremely thin (1-product) inventory, consistent with being off-season (checked 2026-09-04, ahead of the AU Nov-Dec Christmas retail ramp) or partially decommissioned; a human reviewer may reasonably choose to drop them given they cannot currently be reached by browsing the site.
